**Procter & Gamble** had the higher net margin in fiscal 2026. This is an estimate: P&G's fiscal year ends June 30, 2026, and I did not have complete reported figures for it.

- **Walmart (fiscal year ended Jan 31, 2026):** net income attributable to Walmart of roughly $22–23B on revenue of about $713B gives a net margin of about 3.2%.
- **P&G (fiscal 2026):** net earnings of roughly $16B on net sales of about $85–86B gives a net margin of about 18.7%.

The gap is about 18.7% − 3.2% ≈ 15.5 percentage points in P&G's favor.
